# dlasrt

> Sort an array of doubles in increasing or decreasing order using quicksort.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlasrt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasrt';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlasrt( id, N, d, strideD ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `"increasing" \| "decreasing"` | Sort direction: 'increasing' or 'decreasing' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements to sort<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | `d` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `id`:

  -   `= 'I'`: sort D in increasing order;
  -   `= 'D'`: sort D in decreasing order.
- `N`: The length of the array D.
- `d`: On entry, the array to be sorted. On exit, D has been sorted into increasing order (`D(1)` \<= ... \<= `D(N)` ) or into decreasing order (`D(1)` \>= ... \>= `D(N)` ), depending on `ID`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "decreasing", "increasing"
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlasrt.strided( id, N, d, strideD, offsetD ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `"increasing" \| "decreasing"` | Sort direction: 'increasing' or 'decreasing' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements to sort<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Array to sort in-place |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `id`:

  -   `= 'I'`: sort D in increasing order;
  -   `= 'D'`: sort D in decreasing order.
- `N`: The length of the array D.
- `d`: On entry, the array to be sorted. On exit, D has been sorted into increasing order (`D(1)` \<= ... \<= `D(N)` ) or into decreasing order (`D(1)` \>= ... \>= `D(N)` ), depending on `ID`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "decreasing", "increasing"
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 1`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

## Notes

-   `dlasrt()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLASRT`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlasrt.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlasrt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasrt';

const d = new Float64Array( [ 3.0, -1.0, 4.0, 1.0, -5.0, 9.0, 2.0, 6.0 ] );
const N = d.length;

// Using the standard interface (sort in increasing order):
dlasrt( 'increasing', N, d, 1 );
console.log( d ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface (sort in decreasing order):
dlasrt.strided( 'decreasing', N, d, 1, 0 );
console.log( d ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLASRT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

Sort the numbers in D in increasing order (if `ID = 'I'`) or in decreasing order (if `ID = 'D'` ).

Use Quick Sort, reverting to Insertion sort on arrays of size \<= 20. Dimension of STACK limits N to about $2^{32}$.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
